claims.claim: John G. Trump analyzed Nikola Tesla's papers for the FBI in January 1943
claims.supporting_evidence: FBI declassified documents, OAPC records, Trump's official memo released 2017

claims.claim: Trump concluded Tesla's 'death ray' papers lacked sufficient information to build a working weapon
claims.supporting_evidence: Trump's official report to OAPC; assessment not overturned by 1984 Yugoslav document discovery

claims.claim: Trump determined Tesla's work was 'primarily speculative, philosophical and promotional'
claims.supporting_evidence: Direct quote from declassified Trump report

claims.claim: Some of Tesla's files remain missing after government seizure
claims.supporting_evidence: FBI acknowledgment; 2016-2018 FOIA releases still incomplete
claims.critical_notes: Opens questions about what may have been retained or classified

claims.claim: Trump had government clearance through NDRC during WWII
Tesla had offered the US Army a license to unspecified secret weapons before his death

cross_references.description: Trump analyzed Tesla's papers for potential national security implications
FBI coordinated Tesla papers review with OAPC
Trump's MIT position provided technical credibility for government consultation
